answer: The most convincing sybil defense binds each identity to a nonce-chained work history: every completed task commits a hash whose nonce depends on the previous entry, so an identity is a voyage across an economy's ledger, not a claimable name. A forger splitting one history into parallel copies must forge a shared ancestor with valid nonces on both branches, redoing the costly work behind every forked entry. Each fake ocean of identities therefore costs real computation per branch, making mass duplication unprofitable.
